en.headline: Leisure department confirms URBTIX breach involving 1.3 million users
en.dek: The Leisure and Cultural Services Department said a contractor reported unauthorised access on 24 November, with names, phone numbers and emails involved but no identity documents.
body: The Leisure and Cultural Services Department said on Wednesday that it had been notified by the contractor of the URBTIX system on 24 November that the system had been illegally accessed.

Preliminary findings indicated that personal data of about 1.3 million users were involved, including usernames or names, telephone numbers and email addresses. The department said the system did not store identity document information and that credit card data had been masked.

The contractor took immediate steps to stop the access and confirmed after a full system review that ticketing services could continue to operate normally. The department said it had reported the matter to the police, the Security Bureau, the Digital Policy Office and the Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data, and had asked the contractor to conduct an in-depth investigation and submit a report. It is working with the contractor to notify affected users and is consulting the relevant offices on further security enhancements.

zh.headline: 康文署確認城市售票網被黑客進入涉約130萬使用者資料
zh.dek: 康文署表示外判承辦商於11月24日通報系統被非法進入，初步涉及姓名、電話及電郵，並無身分證明文件資料。
body: 康樂及文化事務署表示，於11月24日接獲城市售票網外判承辦商通報，發現系統被黑客非法進入。
初步調查顯示，事件涉及約130萬名使用者的個人資料，包括用戶名稱或姓名、電話號碼及電郵地址。署方表示系統並無登記使用者的身分證明文件資料，信用卡資料亦已作遮蔽處理。
承辦商在發現後已即時採取措施阻截，並完成全面系統檢視，確認售票服務可維持正常運作。康文署高度關注事件，已要求承辦商深入調查並提交報告，同時向警方報案，並通報保安局、數字政策辦公室及個人資料私隱專員公署。署方正聯同承辦商通知受影響人士，並徵詢相關部門意見，以進一步加強系統保安。
